Detailed descriptions of these scenarios and test results are discussed in Section 5. 4 This report is available at no cost from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) at www.nrel.gov/publications 3 Data Center Power System This section describes the data center power system that is modeled in a DRTS platform, along with the data objects that represent critical components for the control of the power flow. A simplified represen- tation of Verrus’s power system is shown in Figure 2, which includes two utility feeds (with breakers X u,1 and X ) connected to a medium-voltage distribution system that provides the power to the downstream u,2 low-voltage IT/computing servers and associated cooling loads. The medium-voltage power distribution has appropriate redundancies in the distribution network design to meet the needs of a high-uptime data center. For this report, only one utility feed is used in normal operation. The feed associated with X is u,1 active, and the feed associated with X is unused. The state of the grid, Grid.State, is considered stable u,2 if the voltage and frequency are within acceptable thresholds, and unstable otherwise. The individual power domains for the IT and compute loads connect to the medium-voltage power distribution through normally closed breakers X ,X ,...,X . Note that a typical data center design would have a redundant power feed for the IT IT,1 IT,2 IT,p loads, but we have not incorporated that because faults/failures are not a focus of this report. The cooling infrastructure/ power domains have mechanical loads such as pumps and chillers, and are connected to the medium-voltage power distribution through the breakers X ,X ,...,X . These breakers are normally c,1 c,2 c,q closed to provide power to the cooling systems. The IT load domains are modeled using a library load component with active power values from an open-source dataset from Google [6]. Each IT load domain, i, can be described as: IT.P=M∗P(k),i={1,2, . . . ,p} i i where IT.P is the active power of the i-th IT load domain, P(k) represents the time-stamped values ob- i i tained from the Google dataset, and M is a multiplier percentage (taking the value of 0% to 100%) to model the optional load shedding initiated by the data center tenant (workload owner). M=100% means NO load shedding, and M=0% means full load shedding. Any intermediate value of M is to be interpreted as shedding the compute load of lower priority.
